## Question of Interest

Is Madison's long-run mean January temperature different in 1995-2024 compared with 1965-1994?

## Data Source

We used US Government Data Catalog to find data sources. It's the GHCN-Daily published by NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information:
<https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/global-historical-climatology-network-daily-ghcn-daily-version-3?from_hint=eyJxIjoiR0hDTi1EYWlseSIsInNvcnQiOiJyZWxldmFuY2UifQ%3D%3D>

According to the GHCNd Station Inventory, the file number for MADISON DANE CO RGNL AP is USW00014837. We downloaded USW00014837.csv from the NCEI Direct Download page and used it as our dataset.

Like to the download page: <https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/global-historical-climatology-network-daily/access/>

Confirm that we can read the data into Rstudio:


```{r}
# Reading the full dataset using the url made knitting slow; so only to confrim that we can access, we just read the first 5 rows and print only 4 columns

weather = read.csv(url("https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/global-historical-climatology-network-daily/access/USW00014837.csv"), nrows = 5)

weather[, c("STATION", "DATE", "TMAX", "TMIN")]
```

## Planned Graph

We will create side-by-side boxplots of the yearly mean January temperature, with one box for each period. This graph can provide a visual comparison of the yearly mean January temperature between the early and recent periods.


## Inference Method

The type of inference method we're going to use is inference on the difference of two population means.

Description: Comparing Madison's mean January temperature in 1995-2024 with 1965-1994. We will test 
$$
H_0: \mu_2 - \mu_1 = 0 \quad \text{versus} \quad H_a: \mu_2 - \mu_1 \neq 0
$$
using a permutation test (pool the 60 yearly January means, randomly reassign them to the two periods many times, and compute the p-value).
